column2: brisk and officious, tapping the ledger, faintly suspicious
sing-song sarcasm, pleased with her own joke
fussy and stern, then a deadpan grudge
shocked and disapproving, then wearily practical
warm and confiding, a little proud of herself
warm, relieved, teasing at the end
proud and fond, with a dry aside
hearty, teasing, a laugh in the voice
expansive, fond, then a joking aside
alarmed, nervous, trying to be polite
worried, lowered voice, gossiping but scared
gruff and grim, remembering, ominous at the end
proud and gruff, laughing at himself
light, amused, then a hint of unease
cheerful, laughing at her own warning
pompous, pleased with his own wit
gravelly, chuckling at his own joke
mock parrot squawk, then grumbling and amused
dry, terse, a hint of pride
